title: Enrollment Terms by Plan Class: Dependents, Injury Claim Numbers, Verification Days and Plan Year — Prescription Insurance on File
content:
When a plan is put on a patient's profile under **Prescription Insurance on File**, the class decides whether dependents may be covered and to what age, whether the employer's injury claim number must be on file before billing, how many calendar days are allowed to confirm eligibility, and what starts the plan year.

| Plan class | Dependents covered | Highest dependent age (whole years) | Injury claim number required | Eligibility verification (calendar days from adding) | Plan year starts |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Medicaid Managed Care Pharmacy Benefit | No | 0 | No | 14 | Calendar year (1 January) |
| Medicare Part D Standard Plan | No | 0 | No | 14 | Calendar year (1 January) |
| Medicare Part D Enhanced Plan | No | 0 | No | 14 | Calendar year (1 January) |
| Medicare Advantage Prescription Drug Plan | No | 0 | No | 14 | Calendar year (1 January) |
| Commercial High-Deductible Health Plan | Yes | 26 | No | 14 | Effective-date anniversary |
| Commercial Copay Plan | Yes | 26 | No | 14 | Effective-date anniversary |
| Workers' Compensation Pharmacy Benefit | No | 0 | Yes | 30 | Effective-date anniversary |

## Terms

- **Dependents covered** — whether dependents may be covered under the cardholder.
- **Highest dependent age** — the highest age in whole years at which a dependent remains covered; 0 when dependents are not covered.
- **Injury claim number required** — whether the employer's injury claim number must be on file before billing.
- **Eligibility verification** — calendar days from adding a plan within which its eligibility must be confirmed.
- **Plan year starts** — calendar year means the plan year runs 1 January to 31 December; effective-date anniversary means it runs from the anniversary of the coverage's effective date to the day before the next anniversary.

## Notes

- Only the two commercial classes cover dependents, up to age 26.
- The Workers' Compensation Pharmacy Benefit alone requires the injury claim number and allows 30 days for eligibility verification; every other class allows 14.

*Example (hypothetical):* a Commercial Copay Plan with an effective date of 15 March runs its plan year from 15 March to 14 March of the following year; a Medicare Part D Standard Plan with the same effective date runs its plan year from 1 January to 31 December.
